Creative walkthrough
This student chooses graphic design after comparing it with digital interface design. Only the supported design pathway is featured; other fields remain available as choices. Visual layouts alone do not imply an interest in public relations.
Fictional development case. Includes shared scripted defaults.

Graphic Designers
Design or create graphics to meet specific commercial or promotional needs, such as packaging, displays, or logos. May use a variety of mediums to achieve artistic or decorative effects.

Why this matches you
Needs confirmation
Your interest profile and work choices connect with this career.

How you like to work
You enjoy working with others. Teamwork matters in this job.
Ask how the team handles busy days and deadlines.
You value original work. Ask where people can propose ideas and improve the way this job is done.
You value independence. Ask which decisions a new employee makes and which need supervision.

Photographers Related match Shares visual ideas and hands-on design work with Graphic Designers.
No college · learn at work
Plan lighting and composition for a client's photographs.
Edit images and manage deadlines and client communication.
Why this matches you
Related match
Shares visual arts and applied arts and design work with Graphic Designers.
How you like to work
Ask how the team handles busy days and deadlines.
You value original work. Ask where people can propose ideas and improve the way this job is done.
You value independence. Ask which decisions a new employee makes and which need supervision.
How to get there
High school or GED, then job training.
Build camera, lighting and editing skills through practice, classes and a portfolio.
No general occupational license.
Useful for photography and business skills
Photography classes build lighting and editing skills. Business classes help with pricing and finding clients.

My saved notes and steps
Build three pieces for a small portfolio
Design a poster, a simple logo and matching colors, and a digital layout. Ask for feedback and revise one piece. Notice whether feedback and changes hold your interest.
My notes
Compare affordable design programs
Compare classes, portfolio requirements, internships, software, cost after grants, and transfer credits. College can build skills and connections; your portfolio still matters for hiring.
My notes
Ask an employed designer about early-career work
Ask about deadlines, client feedback, portfolio expectations, and full-time roles versus freelance hours and business expenses.
My notes
